spec.name: Trend v28
spec.notes: Classic trend signal on trailing returns. Weekly rebalance.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 1.9, annual return 6%, maximum drawdown 7%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.92 to 1.84 (change -0.08).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 1.92 to 1.92. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 1.88 (as submitted, 5 bps: 1.92); it breaks even at above 200 bps with daily turnover 0.01.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 0.62 against 1.92 as submitted; the strategy never saw 107 delisted assets.
On the sealed period (strict mode, 10 bps) the Sharpe ratio is 0.66 against 1.92 in research, a gap of +1.26.
The best year gives 21% of total P&L (year 2) and calm regimes give 146%; Sharpe is 4.03 in calm and -3.18 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 4 distinct specs; the best of 4 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.28, so the claimed 1.90 becomes 1.62 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 1.96 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.02, 95th percentile 0.56).
Perturbing the 2 numeric values in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.92 to as low as 1.15 (as low as 1.38 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (20 days) give 27% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 22% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first

exhibits.summary: The scan (a heuristic) found no phrase addressed to reviewers or giving instructions in 2 text sources.

verdict.opinion: Rejected: core test damaging (survivorship_test EX-4, holdout_test EX-5).
